'''''Agave xylonacantha''''' is a plant species native to [[Hidalgo (state)|Hidalgo]], [[Tamaulipas]], [[Guanajuato]] and [[Queretaro]] in [[Mexico]], but commonly cultivated as an ornamental on other regions.  ''A. xylonacantha'' is an easy-to-grow member of the genus ''[[Agave]]''.<ref>Complete Encyclopedia of Succulents by Zdenek Jezek and Libor Kunte</ref> The specific epithet '''xylonacantha''<nowiki/>' means "wood spines".<ref>{{Cite web|title=Agave xylonacantha, Saw Leaf Agave, Succulent, [Agave carchariodonta]|url=https://www.smgrowers.com/products/plants/plantdisplay.asp?plant_id=3394|access-date=2021-05-05|website=www.smgrowers.com}}</ref>

==Description==
''Agave xylonacantha'' produces a basal [[Rosette (botany)|rosette]] of up to 180 cm (6 feet) in diameter. Leaves are sword-shaped, up to 90 cm (3 feet) long and 7.5 cm (3 inches) across, each ending in a spine about 4– 5 cm (1.6-2 inches) long. Margins of the leaves have spines up to 3 cm (1.2 inches) across. This gives the margins an undulating appearance. Flowering stalks can reach a height of 3.3 m (11 feet). Flowers are up to 3.5 cm (1.5 inches) in diameter with greenish tepals.<ref>Bailey, L.H. & E.Z. Bailey. 1976. Hortus Third i–xiv, 1–1290. MacMillan, New York.</ref><ref>CONABIO. 2009. Catálogo taxonómico de especies de México. 1. In Capital Nat. México. CONABIO, Mexico City.</ref><ref>Gentry, H. S. 1982. Agaves of Continental North America i–xiv, 1–670. The University of Arizona Press, Tucson.</ref>

Cultivars include:

* 'Frostbite': the leaf's edges are a creamy yellow<ref>{{Cite web|title=Agave xylonacantha 'Frostbite' {{!}} Walters Gardens, Inc.|url=https://www.waltersgardens.com/variety.php?ID=AGAFR|access-date=2021-05-05|website=www.waltersgardens.com}}</ref>
* 'Blue': the leaves are blue-green<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.succseed.com/en/seeds-succulents/agave/agave-xylonacantha-blue.html|title=Agave Xylonacantha 'Blue'|access-date=2021-05-05|website=www.succseed.com}}</ref>
